name: 1912 Prairie Avenue — the Moulton/Lowden house (Chateauesque stone front)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B; rear3B stone with brick rear dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Byran P. Moulton Residence. Built 1882'.

research_note: T-3277 (piece 1 of T-1899, the owner's T-1837 Prairie programme) refines the district draft (T-2329) in place under this id onto K01: Byron P. Moulton's 1882 stone house, read off the undated photograph of its front (Chicagology) and the 1883 New Chicago Album vignette against sheet 28's trace. The front from the south: the coped gable with its arched pair, a tall crocketed dormer, the round tower rising three stages to a slated cone, and the north corner block with the door at the high stoop's head under the steep slated roof; behind, the sheet's brick rear ranges. Open for T-3278 and T-1900: the sheet's stone wing on the south flank's rear half, the vignette's and the elevation drawing's cameras, the corbelled corner turret on the north flank, the dormers' and gable's carving, the arched entrance with its awning. Liberty L-k01-1912-moulton-3277.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the marker dates it to 1882 for Byron P. Moulton. The undated photograph (an electric lamp at the curb) and the 1883 album's vignette show the same house.

position.symbolic_location: 1912 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1912 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The front block's rear south corner: the draft's frame point u 0.00, v -1.30 through its own rotation, where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1912-b1 p1) runs the block's south wall (v -1.2 to -1.8 in the draft's frame; its rear half steps out to -3.4 for the stone south wing). The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation -0.622 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1912-b1 p1, '2½B' stone) in the house's frame: its south wall at v 0 (the draft's inscribed 11.75 m rectangle stopped 1.3 m short of it), its north wall at v 13.0, the front at u 20.45 and the rear at u 0. The round bay the sheet draws on the front (v 5.85-9.75, about 1.4 m out) stands on it as a K08 tower, the sheet's two brick ranges behind it as a K01 rear wing. Not built here: the sheet's stone wing on the south flank's rear half (u 0.3-8.9, 2.05 m out), which K01's rear wings (behind the body only) and pavilions (at most 1.2 m out) cannot carry and no picture shows (T-3278).

stories.note: '2½B; rear3B' on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys over a raised basement and a half storey. The photograph shows the half storey as a short third storey of wall across the street front under the cornice (the north corner block's attic window, the tower's third stage, the south gable's attic light), the steep roof rising from its head; the 1883 album's vignette agrees. The brick rear ranges are the sheet's three.

construction.note: The sheet colours the front block stone ('rear3B' brick behind it); the photograph shows coursed ashlar on the front, the north corner block's flank and the round tower.

principal_floor_m.note: The stoop's eleven risers in the photograph (y 1590-1880 px, about 0.17 m each) to the door's sill: about 1.85 m over grade, which K07's stoop and K01's stair both solve in eleven. Barred basement lights stand under the south gable's arched pair.

storey_heights_m.note: Read up the north corner block's front corner in the photograph (x 960 px), where one vertical line keeps one scale (about 92 px a metre, against the door's opening): the principal floor at y 1545 px, the chamber floor's belt at y 1150, the attic floor's dentilled belt at y 750 and the cornice's top at y 495, so 4.3, 4.35 and 2.75 m. The wall head stands near 13.25 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front's thickness at the top of the K01 contract's range; the photograph's reveals are deep but not measurable.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: The stone block's flanks as thick as its front; no picture measures them.

service_wall_brick.note: The kit's K03 panel for the brick rear ranges ('rear3B' brick on the sheet); no picture shows them.

stone_front.note: Coursed smooth ashlar with dressed trim on the photograph's front and flank, with deeper courses at the basement's foot; brown sandstone is the register's brownstone (frontage-28-046), a colour the monochrome print cannot give.

street_front_trim.note: Flat-headed openings under moulded caps on the north corner block, the door and the chamber window over it, and a plain head on its attic window, in the photograph; the south gable's arched pair is its own.

wall_head.note: A moulded stone cornice at the wall head under the slate, round the corner block and the tower's top stage, in the photograph (y 495-530 px).

roof_form.note: A very steep slated roof from the cornice to a short deck with iron cresting over the north corner block, in the photograph and the 1883 vignette; K01's mansard with straight steep faces is that roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck behind the cresting, above every view's sight line.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection past the front in the photograph, about 0.4 m.

mansard.note: The north corner block's roof in the photograph: straight slate faces at about 72 degrees from the cornice to the cresting (y 500-210 px), about 4.5 m through the camera (K01's most for a face over one storey); and two pinnacled stone dormers in the street face: a small one over the corner block's window column (x 340-480, y 290-500 px; built 10.9 m along, 0.5 m south of the column, the nearest the hip lets a dormer stand) and the taller crocketed one between the south gable and the tower (x 740-880, y 150-500 px). Their crockets, pinnacles and carved gables are T-3278's.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the steep faces in the photograph; the deck behind the cresting is the kit's painted tin.

window_kit.note: Two-light sashes with a meeting rail in the windows the ivy leaves open to view.

stair_tread_m.note: The stoop's treads; the photograph shows the flight from its north side.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The landing at the stoop's head under the awning, about 1.5 m before the door, in the photograph.

stoop_width_m.note: The flight between its two solid stone cheek walls, about 2.2 m against the door's width, in the photograph and the vignette.

entrance_bay.note: The door in the north corner block, under its chamber window and dormer, beside the round tower, in the photograph and the 1883 vignette, read against the sheet's bay.

front_bays.note: One opening column in the north corner block (v 9.75-13.0, north of the sheet's bay at v 5.85-9.75): the door at the stoop's head with the chamber and attic windows over it, in the photograph (door x 720-880 px, windows x 760-870 px).

side_bays.note: The south flank toward 1918; no picture shows it.

north_bays.note: The north flank: the window column the photograph shows under the corbelled corner turret (x 1060-1120 px), which the photograph's camera (T-3277) puts at s 2.6-4.0 from the front corner, so at s 2.8 under the turret's axis (T-3290; first read as s 1.7); the two behind it are reconstructed. The attic light of that column is the turret's own.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall above the brick ranges; no picture shows the rear.

sash_by_storey.note: The corner block's chamber window about 1.1 x 2.7 m (x 760-870, y 862-1112 px, its sill 0.4 m over the belt) and its attic window about 0.9 x 1.6 m (y 530-700 px; built 1.35 m, its head under the cornice's bed); the flanks' principal windows about 1.15 x 2.9 m.

basement_lights.note: The barred basement lights under the south gable's arched pair in the photograph (x 80-240, y 1610-1700 px).

chimneys.note: The tall panelled stone stack rising off the north flank behind the corner block in the photograph (x 1090-1190 px, its cap at y 120 px), and a second on the sheet's chimney breast on the south flank (u 12.3-15.7), which no picture shows.

rainwater.note: K01's copper gutter behind the cornice and two downpipes; no picture shows them.

entrance_kit.note: The door at the stoop's head in the north corner block, in the photograph and the vignette; the stoop's solid stone cheek walls end in block newels at the foot. T-1900: the door stands in a deep round-arched recess, as the photograph (x 720-890, y 1195-1545 px, the arch's crown just over the awning at y 1205-1225 px, about 3.4 m over the principal floor through the solved camera) and the 1883 plate draw it, and as the c. 1914 elevations drawing heads it: a pair of panelled leaves 0.6 m back in a 1.7 m arch, under a 0.3 m voussoir ring with a moulded edge and a keystone that stops under the chamber floor's belt. The mouth's width is the kit's (the photograph's pilasters stand about 1.9 m apart, read across a foreshortened front); the leaves, the reveal's depth and the moulding are reconstructed, in L-k01-1912-moulton-entrance-1900. The carved capitals on the pilasters either side, and the striped canvas awning (a seasonal fitting, kept off the 1904 build), are not built.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the tower's tall principal lights in the photograph, about 2.9 m against the door
the tower's chamber lights in the photograph, level with the corner block's (y 862-1112 px)
the third stage's short lights under the cone in the photograph (y 580-710 px)

the gable's principal pair in the photograph (x 95-265, y 1290-1545 px) and the 1883 plate: two lights, each under its own round head glazed as a fanlight over a one-over-one sash, either side of a stone mullion, under one arch (T-1900: built round-headed; the enclosing arch over the pair is not built, a remaining difference on both match records)
the gable's chamber pair in the photograph

the attic light at the gable's foot, in the photograph (x 170-240, y 670-820 px; built 0.6 m of its 1.5, inside the gable storey's clear wall, the rest standing in the gable's face, where K08 cuts no light)

the corner turret's one light, about 0.65 x 1.45 m in the photograph (x 1063-1107, y 595-725 px), narrower than the flank's sashes so it stands on the turret's face; built 1.25 m tall under the turret's lowered wall top

bays.note: Two K08 pieces on the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1912-b1) in the house's frame, read with the photograph and the 1883 vignette. The round tower on the sheet's front bulge (v 5.85-9.75, about 1.4 m out; built a 1.95 m round centred 0.17 m in front of the wall line, so 0.72 m further out than the sheet draws it, the least that holds its finial clear of the wall's plane): three stages of bent sashes to a slated cone with a plain finial (the photograph's is turned, with knobs: an open difference on the match record), its third stage 1.0 m taller than the photograph's, whose cone springs at the main cornice's level, because K01 stands a tower's wall top at least 1.0 m over its host's eave. The south gable (v 0.5-4.1): a stone projection 0.4 m proud (the sheet draws the front flush there, under its resolution), the least that holds its windows' recesses, cut to the kit's 0.33 m minimum, in front of the wall with its arched pair, its chamber pair and its attic light, its coped gable with pinnacles and a finial rising from just over the attic floor (its kneelers at y 720 px, under the main cornice) to an apex near 14 m (y 470 px). T-3290: the corbelled corner turret on the north flank (`north_turret`), read off the photograph through its solved camera (x 1050-1145 px, the flank's front corner at x 960): a round oriel 1.4 m across, its centre on the wall's plane at s 2.8 from the front corner (its two silhouettes land within 6 px of the photograph's), standing on the attic floor (10.5 m) on a turned stone foot where the photograph's attic belt sweeps round it (y 745-800 px), one storey with one light turned toward the avenue (x 1063-1107, y 595-725 px), under a moulded stone cornice and a steep slated cone (pitch 3.0, to about 15.7 m) that leans on the mansard as the photograph's leans on its slate and its stack (y 365-520 px). Its wall top is 12.25 m, about 0.55 m under the photograph's (whose turret cornice runs level with the main cornice), because K01 holds an oriel's wall top a metre under the main eave unless the eave dies into it, which the kit does only on a street front under a hip or gable: an open difference on the match record. The 1883 plate draws it taller, two stages corbelled out from the chamber floor; the photograph's one stage over the attic belt is built, and the disagreement is within tolerance on the plate's match record.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's two brick ranges behind the front block ('rear3B'; s28fp-1912-b1 p2 and p3, u -7.4 to -0.4 and v 0 to 12.7 in the house's frame) as one three-storey brick wing under a flat tin roof; its storeys, windows and roof are reconstructed: no picture shows the rear.

boundary.note: A low iron railing on a stone coping along the walk in the photograph (y 1700-1780 px), open at the stoop's foot; the lot's sides are the 1904 parcel's (data/street_grid/1904.json). The gates are reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1912-moulton-3277).

yard.note: The walk in flags from the stoop's foot through the railing's opening to the public walk, and the cinder service walk from the side gate back along the south lot line.
